overview: White plays a quiet anti-Sicilian with 2.b3, aiming for Bb2 on the long diagonal against e5/g7, then Nf3, e3 or f4, and a flexible centre. Black usually responds 2...Nc6, 2...d6 or 2...e6 and takes a normal Sicilian set-up, using the extra space and the half-open c-file. The play is quiet and manoeuvring with little theory, and Black often equalises easily.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bb2, Nf3, e3 and Bb5 to pressure e5 and the long diagonal
Choose a central plan with c4, d4 or f4 after seeing Black's set-up
Keep the position flexible and avoid Open Sicilian theory

black_ideas.idea: Play ...Nc6, ...e5 or ...d6 and ...Nf6 for a solid centre
Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7 to contest the long diagonal
Use the half-open c-file and queenside expansion

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian with White's e4 and b3 fianchetto against Black's ...c5, ...d6, ...e5 or ...e6

character.notes: Quiet manoeuvring play with little theory; Black is not under pressure.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black an easy game; White's centre is undeveloped.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed; White's e4 against Black's ...c5 and a flexible pawn structure.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly choose it; it is chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Few moves to learn but plans need judgement; not Beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...b6 mirror
sublines_that_differ.how: Black mirrors with a queen fianchetto and the play is symmetrical.

character.reason: Quiet and flexible, neither forcing nor especially hard to break.

structure.reason: No fixed centre; flank fianchetto play.

level.reason: Few lines but plans need judgement.
